summary: Innovation (3/5): draws on satellite applied to a disaster management problem, placing it in the moderate band. detail.title: AI/ML-Based Nowcasting of Thunderstorm and Lightning

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a system that predicts thunderstorms and lightning strikes in the next few hours, combining data from multiple radars, satellites, and lightning detectors, so warnings arrive with enough lead time to actually matter.
overview.why_it_matters: Thunderstorms and lightning develop fast. Short-term, accurate nowcasting is what makes the difference between a useless warning after the fact and one people can actually act on.
pain_points: Thunderstorm and lightning events develop rapidly, needing very short-term prediction, not just general forecasting.
Multiple data sources (radar, satellite, lightning networks, model data) aren't currently integrated for real-time nowcasting.
Existing forecasting timescales may not give sufficient actionable lead time for fast-developing convective events.
overview.background: Thunderstorms and lightning pose real safety and operational risks and develop on short timescales, requiring integrated nowcasting (very short-term prediction) using multiple real-time atmospheric observation sources. Verified against the official SIH26072 portal listing (Ministry of Earth Sciences / IMD) — the description above matches the official text (title and description are effectively identical in the source), not an inference gap.
overview.whats_being_asked: An AI/ML nowcasting system for thunderstorms and lightning using multiple radars, satellite, lightning detection networks, and model data.
expected_solution: Real-time integration of multi-radar, satellite, and lightning data.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Moderate. Convective nowcasting is an established meteorological ML research area, the value is in genuine multi-source integration (radar plus satellite plus lightning network) rather than a single-source approach.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Moderate. Achievable using established nowcasting techniques (radar extrapolation, ML-based convective initiation prediction) with public or simulated multi-source data.

competitive_landscape.note: Weather nowcasting is a recognizable category among the many MoES weather PS in this batch, differentiation depends on genuine multi-source integration and short lead-time accuracy.

innovation.note: Established nowcasting technique category, value is in genuine multi-source integration for this specific application.

invention.note: Achievable using established radar-extrapolation or ML-based convective prediction approaches.

technical_feasibility.note: Public radar and lightning network data exist for many regions, providing real data for training and testing.

impact_and_benefits.note: Short-term severe weather warnings have direct, immediate safety value for affected populations.

architecture.note: Multi-source data fusion feeding a nowcasting model, a well-understood integration pattern.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick, genuinely achievable with real public radar and lightning data, though it sits alongside several similar MoES weather nowcasting PS in this batch, differentiation should come from genuine multi-source fusion quality, not just picking one data type.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Public radar and lightning detection network data genuinely exist for real training and testing, not synthetic substitutes.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Using only one data source (e.g. just radar) while claiming 'multi-source integration' would be a shallow interpretation of the actual PS ask, genuine fusion across radar, satellite, and lightning data is the differentiator.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Commit to genuinely integrating at least two distinct data source types (e.g. radar plus lightning network data) rather than a single-source model relabeled as multi-source nowcasting.

idea_0_4: Source public radar and lightning detection network data for a test region and time period with known thunderstorm activity.
Choose your nowcasting approach: radar-echo extrapolation combined with lightning-occurrence correlation is a reasonable, genuinely multi-source starting point.
Split: one person on radar data processing, one on lightning data integration and the prediction model.
prototype_4_22: Build your radar data processing and echo-tracking/extrapolation pipeline.
Build your lightning-data integration, correlating lightning occurrence patterns with radar-observed convective development.
Start your nowcasting prediction model combining both data sources.
integration_22_30: Connect radar and lightning data fusion into one coherent short-term prediction pipeline.
Test against a real known thunderstorm event in your test region/period, comparing your prediction against actual documented occurrence and timing.
Measure your actual lead time, how far in advance did your system flag the developing storm.
polish_30_36: Build a clear visualization showing your nowcast prediction against real radar/lightning observations over your test event.
Rehearse presenting your real lead-time and accuracy results.
Prepare to discuss how genuine multi-source fusion improved your prediction versus a single-source baseline.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show your system's prediction timeline against a real historical thunderstorm event, with your predicted development timing compared to when the storm actually occurred, real lead-time evidence is the core value proposition of nowcasting.

strengths: Public radar and lightning data genuinely available for real training and validation.
Clear, measurable success criteria (actual lead time achieved) for a concrete demo.
weaknesses: Sits among several similar weather-nowcasting PS in this batch, genuine multi-source fusion is needed to differentiate.
Short-timescale prediction accuracy is inherently harder to validate convincingly than longer-range forecasting.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Balanced across radar and lightning data specialization, genuine fusion is the differentiator.
team_fit.approach: Source real historical data for a known thunderstorm event first, this gives you a concrete validation target from the start rather than building blind.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Standard radar-echo extrapolation and nowcasting model scaffolding.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Designing a genuine fusion approach that meaningfully combines radar and lightning signals (not just running them as separate, unconnected models), that's real system-design judgment.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-scaffolded single-source nowcaster relabeled as 'multi-source' without genuine data fusion would miss the actual differentiating ask and likely underperform a properly integrated system.

data_resource_availability.status: Public radar and lightning detection network data genuinely exist for many regions, allowing real training and validation.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not needed, real data access is achievable, choosing a well-documented historical thunderstorm event maximizes validation credibility.

judge_qna.question: How does combining radar and lightning data actually improve your prediction versus using just one source?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Present a direct comparison, your fused model's performance against a single-source baseline on the same test event, quantifying the improvement from genuine data fusion.
judge_qna.follow_up: Which data source contributed more to prediction accuracy, and in what situations?

judge_qna.question: What's your actual achieved lead time, and is that operationally useful?
judge_qna.strong_answer: State your measured lead time from real historical validation directly, and compare it against what's generally considered operationally actionable for thunderstorm warnings.
judge_qna.follow_up: How does your lead time vary across different types of convective events?
